title: Chimichurri With Oregano
description: Michelle Bernstein's mother taught her how to make this recipe when she was five years old because it is such an essential part of Argentinean cuisine; a bowl of chimichurri can be found on every dinner table. In her home base of Miami, the award-winning chef is known for her expert cooking with Latin flavors. Super tasty, traditional and incredibly easy to make, her recipe features fresh parsley, garlic and tangy vinegar. It gets an extra kick from oregano and crushed red pepper. Chimichurri is typically served with steak, but it's also great on smoky grilled fish and chicken.
ingredients: Kosher salt and freshly ground pepper
1 1/2 tablespoons (or more) crushed red pepper flakes
2/3 cup (or more) olive or sunflower oil
directions: In a food processor, combine the parsley, vinegar, garlic, oregano and crushed red pepper. (Maybe add the whole garlic first, with the machine running, to mince it finely.)
Process until smooth; season with salt and pepper.
Add the olive oil and give it a couple of quick pulses.
Transfer to a serving dish and let stand for at least 20 minutes.
Spoon this herbaceous, garlicky sauce over any grilled steak (like skirt steak).

Combine 1/3 cup dried oregano and 1 1/2 Tbsp. crushed red pepper flakes in a small bowl. Add 1 cup warm water and massage mixture with your hands. Let stand until oregano and pepper flakes are softened and water is absorbed, about 15 minutes.
Add 1/2 cup chopped flat-leaf parsley, 4 minced garlic cloves, and 1/2 tsp. kosher salt.
Stir in 2/3 cup (or more) olive or sunflower oil; let stand for at least 1 hour or chill for up to 2 days to let the flavors meld.
Season sauce to taste with red wine vinegar and more garlic, salt, or oil, if desired.
